script.opening_words: The advice you actually follow costs $5 a day. The decision that decides your net worth got 11 minutes in a dealership parking lot. You know the drill. You canceled the streaming subscriptions. You have a chest freezer in the garage for bulk chicken. You own a label maker and you have labeled things that did not need labeling. You have been careful for years in exactly the ways you were told. And you are about to sign something at
script.ending_words: advice. It is arithmetic and arithmetic does not know your circumstances. If you want to dive deeper, check out our school community using the link below. But if you keep one thing from this, keep this. Before you accept any piece of money advice, ask who it costs nothing to give. Free advice is almost always aimed at your change jar. Nobody has ever put the vault in a headline.
script.analysis: Full 16856 canonical characters read. Narrative myth-busting essay with three personas (Julie, Otis, Andrea): BLS spending shape, carrying-a-balance myth, rent vs own, waiting for the dip / all-time highs, Dalbar behaviour gap critique, active vs index fees, new-car opportunity cost, emotional section, Social Security fear, whole life, latte factor resolved, close. Unusually well-sourced for the channel: BLS 2024, G.19 22.15%, Vanguard 68%, SPIVA 79% and Trustees 2033/77% verify; most arithmetic reproduces. Errors: the 1% fee scenario ($2.99M/$820K vs $2.87M/$902K reproduced); simple-interest card cost; several statistics not fetched. Stored ending complete.
beat_map: Intro and filter: myths survive because cheap.
Julie: rent vs own; housing returns and costs.
Andrea: all-time highs, lump sum, best days, cash cost.
Otis: new car payments and opportunity cost.
